To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the health status of MA enrollees is more favorable than that of traditional Medicare enrollees and that the health status differences between the two populations are large enough to explain most, if not all, of the differences in payments between the programs.

Medicare Advantage (MA) plans receive higher risk‐adjusted payments than they would receive under the alternative risk adjustment methods we studied, and that the higher payments are driven by higher risk‐adjusted payment levels for plans with higher market shares and for plans with higher enrollment of beneficiaries with low socioeconomic status (SES).

Medicare Advantage (MA) plans received higher risk‐adjusted payments in 2009 than they would have under a benchmarking approach based on a risk adjustment model that uses only the same clinical risk factors as the MA risk adjustment model and the same payment rate for each risk group.

the Medicare Advantage plans are not paying more than the average cost of the Medicare beneficiaries and the Medicare Advantage plans have been providing better care and services than the fee for services Medicare beneficiaries.

the MA plans are not paying more for beneficiaries who are sicker than the fee‐for‐service population, but the risk‐adjusted payments do not fully compensate the MA plans for the higher costs of beneficiaries with multiple chronic conditions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Medicare Advantage (MA) plans receive risk‐adjusted payments that are generally similar in size to those that would have been received under the traditional Medicare fee‐for‐service (FFS) program.
the Medicare Advantage (MA) program is not a good way to pay for health care for beneficiaries, and that it does not save Medicare money.
the Medicare Advantage (MA) program has not been successful in improving health outcomes for beneficiaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Medicare Advantage (MA) plans are paid for risk adjustment scores that are higher than scores for beneficiaries with the same demographic characteristics and medical conditions in the traditional Medicare fee‐for‐service (FFS) program.

risk‐based payments to Medicare Advantage plans are not closely aligned with the health risk of their beneficiaries, and that there are alternative measures of risk that would better align payments with beneficiary health risk.
Medicare’s current payment system for Medicare Advantage (MA) plans is not risk adjusted to the degree that it could be.
